Manuela is a straight up gem in the middle of LA and I don’t say that lightly. Walking in through the Hauser & Wirth complex you immediately feel it open, fresh, artistic, like the city took a breath. The kind of place that makes you slow down without even trying.

We got the burrata salad and the dressing is what got me. Just perfectly balanced and bright, letting the burrata actually shine.

And the biscuits? Everything people say and more. Buttery, rich, the kind you tear into and immediately want another. Not overly heavy, just deeply satisfying.

Service was excellent  attentive without being in your face, which is exactly what you want when the environment is this good and you just want to sit in it.

One honest note  the venison burger didn’t quite land for us, and if you’re someone who prioritizes protein options, the menu is a little limited on that front.

Would love to see them expand there.

Other than that, it’s casual but elevated  you don’t feel like you have to perform, you just get to enjoy. If you’re in LA and haven’t been, add it to the list. It feeds you in more ways than one.

text.text:
Manuela in the Arts District is exactly the kind of restaurant that makes downtown Los Angeles feel layered, creative and alive. Tucked inside the Hauser & Wirth complex, it is not just a place to eat, but a full experience — part restaurant, part garden, part art-world escape.

The setting is easily one of its biggest strengths. You walk into a space where the art, open kitchen, patio, greenery and industrial Arts District character all come together without feeling forced. There is a calmness to the restaurant that makes it feel special, but not stiff.

The food leans modern American with a strong Southern influence, and the menu clearly celebrates seasonal produce, local farms and ingredient-led cooking. Among the starters, the cream biscuits were exceptional — warm, comforting, beautifully made and honestly one of those dishes that can set the tone for the whole meal. They are the kind of simple thing that only works when the execution is really strong.

What I enjoyed most about Manuela is that it has a point of view. The restaurant does not feel like it is chasing trends. It knows what it is: seasonal, relaxed, artistic, rooted in California produce, but with a Southern comfort thread running through the food. The menu moves comfortably between shareable starters, seafood, vegetables, wood-fired dishes and cocktails, making it a great place for brunch, lunch, dinner or even a slower afternoon meal in the Arts District.

Overall, Manuela is one of those LA restaurants where the environment and the food support each other beautifully. It is stylish without being cold, thoughtful without being precious, and memorable without trying too hard. I would go back for the setting, the garden, the atmosphere — and absolutely for those biscuits.

text.text:
Guisados in Downtown LA may look unassuming from the outside, but it ended up being the best Mexican meal we had during our entire trip to the US. The moment the food arrived, it was clear this place focuses on quality above everything else.

I ordered the 6 mini taco sampler, which offers smaller portions of their regular tacos. Altogether it works out to roughly the size of two and a half full tacos, and every single one was packed generously with flavourful fillings. The Cochinita Pibil and the Frijoles with Queso were real standouts, each with its own bold, rich taste.

The Quesadilla con Chorizo was another highlight, perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. My drink, the Armando Palmero, was incredibly refreshing and bursting with flavour. Our server recommended it, and her suggestion was spot on. She provided excellent service throughout the meal, friendly, helpful, and clearly proud of the food they serve.

This spot is a true gem, and I would recommend it wholeheartedly to anyone visiting Downtown LA.

Vaca DTLA nestled in Downtown Los Angeles, transports diners to the vibrant culinary scene of Spain. From the moment you step inside, you’re greeted by a bold and refined dining experience that promises to tantalize your taste buds.

The star of the show is their house specialty, the Prime Ribeye Steak. Aged to perfection for 50 days, this steak boasts a deep, rich flavor that melts in your mouth. Accompanying it are the Gambas al Ajillo, a sizzling dish of prawns sautéed in olive oil, garlic, and chili flakes. They pair perfectly with the warm, crusty grilled bread.

The Paella de Mariscos is the true centerpiece of the menu. This seafood paella is a symphony of flavors, featuring an abundance of prawns, clams, mussels, octopus, and saffron bomba rice. It’s finished with a silky garlic aioli that adds a touch of creaminess and elevates the dish to new heights.

To complement the vibrant Spanish flavors, Vaca DTLA offers their signature cocktail, The Vaca Tonic. Crafted with Brooklyn Gin, a frozen gimlet, Fever Tree Mediterranean tonic, and a fragrant basil blossom, this refreshing and aromatic cocktail is the perfect accompaniment to your meal.

Vaca DTLA brings a beautiful taste of Spain right to the heart of Downtown Los Angeles, offering a dining experience that is both authentic and unforgettable.

I genuinely don't think I could have done the meat the same justice.

Additional shout-out to Aidan and Joseph. They took great care of me and ensured I had a premium meal.

text.text:
Niku X is such a cute little upstairs spot tucked inside a fancy restaurant—definitely gives that elevated, special-occasion vibe right when you walk in.

I really appreciated how the staff took the time to clearly explain my Chubby Cattle membership. Turns out it only applied to one location, so I had to upgrade—but honestly, the upgrade worked out in my favor since it gave me a better discount than the other offer I had been texted. That level of transparency was a huge plus.

Service across the board was amazing. Everyone was welcoming, attentive, and on top of everything all night. They absolutely do not lack in service by any means.

That said… I was a bit let down by the seafood. Based on reviews and Instagram photos, I came in with high expectations. The king crab legs were noticeably smaller than expected and unfortunately a bit dry when eating them. The standout for me was definitely the colossal shrimp—those were excellent. The steamed lobster was good, but not quite great.

One small suggestion: it would really improve the experience if they either trimmed the underside of the lobster shell so it’s easier (and safer) to hold, or pre-loosened the meat from the shell after slicing it open. It was a bit of a struggle to get to the meat, even though the flavor itself was solid.

Since I went on my birthday, I did get a larger discount, which was a big win and honestly one of the main reasons we chose to go tonight.

Overall, I’d say it’s worth trying—especially for a celebration—but probably not somewhere I’d go just for a casual night out.

* Truffled Mushroom Pizza 5/5 - This was delicious in a way I didn't expect. The pizza was fluffy and crispy at the same time. The truffle aioli sauce was flavorful. The mushrooms were enjoyable as well.

* Grilled Shrimp Skewer 4/5 - Tasted good, a bit salty.

* Dragon fruit Cosmo 5/5 - Nice sweet drink. Tasted strong due to the Skyy Vodka. The dehydrated dragon fruit added an interesting touch.

* Mac & Cheese 4/5 - This was pretty good.

I recently visited Bossa Nova Brazilian Restaurant, and overall, it was a solid experience.
The highlight of the visit was definitely the service. The staff was genuinely great—attentive, friendly, and very welcoming. The restaurant itself has a good atmosphere and is quite spacious, with plenty of seating available, so you likely won't feel cramped or have to wait long for a table.
As for the food, it was good, but I wouldn't necessarily say it was the greatest Brazilian restaurant I’ve been to. It hits the spot, and a massive bonus is that they keep a full kitchen open late. If you are looking for a proper, sit-down meal late at night, this is a fantastic option.
A quick heads-up: Street parking is pretty limited in the area, so you might need to circle the block a bit or plan ahead for where to leave your car.

The Rundown:
Pros: Fantastic staff, good vibe, full late-night menu, lots of seating.
Cons: Food is solid but not mind-blowing; parking can be a hassle.

I'd definitely return, especially for a late-night bite!

This was definitely an experience.

As someone not from the West Coast, driving into the area felt a little unexpected for a Michelin-recognized spot. It’s tucked inside a food hall with minimal signage, so just look for the line on the right when you walk in.

I went on a weekday about an hour before closing, so the wait was pretty minimal.

The menu is so good it’s hard to choose, so I didn’t. I ordered one of each type of dish. Tacos (the kanpachi taco was the standout), tuna tostada, scallop aguachile, yellowtail ceviche, coctel de camarón, and sea urchin. The uni wasn’t for me, and just a heads up, it’s served very fresh, like still moving when it hits the table.

Everything tasted incredibly fresh and well executed. It felt authentic without trying too hard, which I appreciated.

The staff was friendly and the whole process ran smoothly, even in a busy food hall setting.

text.text:
TL;DR: Worth the hype, the line, and possibly a small emotional commitment.

We finally made it to Holbox this past weekend, and wow—consider us officially late to the party and very glad we showed up. We rolled up to Mercado La Paloma around 6:30 pm on a Friday, mentally preparing for a “stand here and question your life choices” kind of line… but plot twist: it moved fast! We were inside in about 15 minutes, which was just enough time to stare intensely at the menu and pretend we’re decisive people.

We went all in and ordered Scallop Aguachile, Bluefin Tuna Tostadas, Baja Fish Tacos, Grilled Branzino, and Grilled Octopus. Everything was fantastic. If I had to crown a winner (and I do), it’s the Grilled Octopus with Almond Pipian sauce. It was so good I briefly considered ordering a second one “for research.”

The market vibe is super chill—casual, lively, and just chaotic enough to be fun. The staff from all restaurants, not just Holbox, do a great job clearing tables, so finding a place to sit wasn’t an issue. We never had to awkwardly hover behind diners, making intense eye contact and willing them to leave.

Bonus perk of the food hall situation: snack diversification. We grabbed a couple of aguas frescas from Oaxacalifornia because hydration is important when you’re this committed to eating everything in sight.

Service was friendly and efficient, with staff constantly circulating, making it easy to ask questions and—most importantly—secure dessert. Speaking of which: chocolate and churros were ordered with zero hesitation, plus two more orders to go!

Final verdict: We will definitely be back to try more of Holbox’s menu!

This little downtown diner is beautiful. I love the art deco aesthetic and for me it is especially fun to revisit downtown because I used to live there for a couple years. It’s located on the ground floor of a high-rise and as mentioned it’s really beautifully designed with a very large bar and a long row of booths and tables to choose from. They also have a very large private outdoor eating area as well so they have plenty of seating options. Parking in this area isn’t too bad, they offer a valet in front or it’s not hard to find street parking on the street the back. Our server was very polite and everything that we ordered came out surprisingly fast.

This was my first visit and it took me a minute to decide what I wanted to get because the menu is not very large, but has some great options on it. I ended up choosing the Chilaquiles. I thought they were very good and I enjoyed it very much, however, I wish there would’ve been a protein component to it because after a while it was just all chips. Aside from that the eggs were done perfectly and I would recommend.

text.text:
We dined at La Perla Ristorante during the Dine LA Restaurant Week experience while celebrating an anniversary, and the evening unfortunately took a very serious turn.

The food quality was very subpar. The starters were overly salty, the meat courses were overcooked, and overall the dishes lacked the level of care and execution one would expect from an upscale Italian restaurant - particularly during a Dine LA menu that is meant to showcase the kitchen at its best.

More concerning was how a severe allergy was handled. We informed the staff in advance of this allergy, yet a member of our group experienced a reaction during the meal. This was extremely distressing and caused us to leave promptly for health and safety reasons. Given the circumstances, we left a $0 tip, which was communicated at the time and directly related to the allergy incident and how it was handled - not out of negligence or bad faith.

Two days later, after checking my bank statement, I discovered that an additional ~$40 tip had been added without my consent or prior disclosure, despite the fact that no tip had been left due to the incident. This was never communicated at the time of payment and removed any opportunity to address it in the moment.

In an effort to resolve this directly and in good faith, we returned to the restaurant to give management an opportunity to address the situation and explain this billing practice. The response we received was simply, “Oops, it was a mistake,” with no further explanation, accountability, or meaningful attempt to address the seriousness of the issue. Given the circumstances-an allergy-related incident and an unauthorized charge-we expected a far more thoughtful and responsible response.

We expect transparency in billing, serious handling of food allergies, and a higher standard of accountability from an upscale restaurant, especially during a featured dining event. Experiences like this erode trust, and we hope management takes this feedback seriously and reviews both their service and billing practices moving forward.

There’s a reason Drago Centro has remained one of the most respected Italian restaurants in Los Angeles for so many years. The moment you walk in, you can feel the legacy, elegance, and passion behind this place.

★★★★☆

I was very pleased with both the food and the atmosphere. Bavel has an energetic vibe, beautiful design, and every dish that came to the table was thoughtfully presented.

We started with the appetizers, and the duck hummus was the star of the night. It was so unbelievably good that we ordered a second one. Paired with the warm, house-made pita, it was hands down my favorite dish of the entire meal. The grilled octopus was another standout—perfectly tender with a delicious smoky char.

For the main course, every dish was outstanding. The crispy quail had an incredible crunch while remaining tender and juicy. The lamb neck literally melted in your mouth and was one of the most memorable dishes of the evening. The bone-in ribeye was cooked perfectly, with a beautiful crust, rich marbling, and deep, beefy flavor that made it ideal for sharing. The grilled shrimp were large, fresh, and perfectly seasoned with just the right amount of char, complementing the other dishes without overpowering them.

Dessert was the perfect ending to the evening. The sticky date cake was warm, rich, and paired beautifully with the ice cream. The pavlova was light and airy with fresh berries that balanced the sweetness perfectly. We also had the warm chocolate-filled doughnuts with caramel ice cream, which were decadent, indulgent, and impossible not to love. Every dessert was beautifully executed and absolutely worth saving room for.

The only disappointment was the service. While everyone was friendly, the service was below expectations for a restaurant of this caliber. Throughout the evening, the servers consistently seemed to rush us, making us feel like they were trying to turn the table rather than allowing us to relax and fully enjoy the experience.

Overall, Bavel serves some of the best food I’ve had in Los Angeles. The duck hummus alone is worth the visit, and I’ll definitely be back for the incredible cuisine and atmosphere. I just hope the service becomes more focused on letting guests enjoy the experience at their own pace.

We accidentally had the dineLA experience for our party of 11 celebrating a birthday. The birthday girl chose this place as she remembered loving her previous visit. Most of us had never been.

It was after we checked in that we found out they were offering the dineLA menu. Shockingly, they didn’t make the whole table partake like how other places I’ve been to require it. 9 of us opted for it.
To backtrack a little, we were originally a party of 12 that became 11 on the day of dinner. As our arrivals scattered, the host said he could only seat us once 8 people were there. Some sat by the waiting area and some of us went to the bar. We got there just as happy hour had ended, but the bartender let us order from the HH menu since we got there just in time. S/O to the bartender.

First off, my drinks were amazing. The presentation was 10/10.
The food was amazing. I think I was one of a few that didn’t have any takeaway. I went to town on all the ones I picked.
We started with the cucumbers and potato salad. I could legitimately eat that combo for the rest of my days. My friend ended up getting another order of the potato to take home. I wish I did the same. My app was the tartare tacos. I kilt that
For my main, I went with the nigiri platter. The rice was so good that I couldn’t stop talking about it. I was able to try the short rib that the person next to me ordered and wow. Perfect spices. It was so yummy. I ended with the gelato/sorbet combo. Truth be told, the cheesecake was far better.
I will however say that overall I had no notes regarding all the foods. Same for the cocktails.

Despite all that, I’m giving them 3/5 because the service was wild. Our server was Ryan?
Here’s what I’ve noticed in the LA area, when your party is a certain # where gratuity is automatically added to the bill, the service tends to be disappointing. It’s like they don’t even try to put in the least knowing they’re getting 20% guaranteed.
Our server was MIA when we needed something. I don’t remember him checking in on us. And let me tell you something, the man dining solo next to us as well as the party of 2 (grandma/grandson)  directly behind us spent a majority of their time looking for our server.

To end on a positive, the live band was fantastic. The singer had a great voice and sang a ton of our favorites.

Retro music when we were there and it would be a great place for a night out for drinks or a meal. While there were some who were dressed to the nines, we were not and felt comfortable being there. Be sure to check this place out!
